chunks: Al-Kafi: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad; and Sahl ibn Ziyad; and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all together, from Ibn Mahbub, from Jamil ibn Salih, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

What prevents a merchant among you who is busy in his marketplace from, when he returns to his home, not sleeping until he recites a Chapter from the Qur'an? So it will be written for him, in place of every verse he recites, ten good deeds, and ten evil deeds will be effaced for him.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting the Qur'an before sleeping for a busy merchant?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi emphasizes the importance of maintaining spiritual discipline amidst the distractions of trade, specifically instructing busy merchants to recite a Surah before sleep. It highlights the tangible spiritual economy of the hereafter, where each verse yields a multiplier of ten good deeds and erases ten sins, reinforcing the concept of consistent, small acts of worship. This practice serves as a daily reset for the soul, ensuring that worldly engagements do not sever the connection with the Divine.
